transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in today because... it's just been so unsettling lately. Even on my better days, when I have a little more energy, I just can't shake this feeling that some of the people at my church, and also in my senior walking club, are watching me. 

We meet on Tuesdays for the walking club, usually over at the community center track unless it's raining. Last week it just poured, absolutely came down in buckets, so we had to walk the indoor loop. That concrete floor is just so hard on my knees. I've been telling them for months we should just go walk the mall when it rains, they open the doors early just for walkers, you know? But Brenda insists on the community center because she likes the parking there. 

Anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right. I just feel like they're keeping an eye on me. And they keep putting these little messages about me in the Sunday church bulletin, or hiding things in what they say when we're doing our laps. I just don't understand why they're doing it.
Do you believe that the messages in the church bulletin or the things people say during your walks are specifically directed at you or have a special meaning for you?

Yes, exactly. I know it might sound silly to say out loud, but I really do believe those messages are meant just for me. Like I was saying, even on my better days, I just can't shake this feeling that they are watching me, and then they put these little hints in the bulletin or in what they say to me on the track. 

The bulletin last Sunday... well, first of all, they started printing it on this awful bright yellow paper. Our old church secretary, Martha, she always used a lovely cream cardstock. It was so much easier on the eyes, very elegant. But Martha moved to Ohio a few years ago to be with her daughter. Cleveland, I think? Or maybe Cincinnati. I could never do the snow up there. My sister lived in Michigan for a while and she said the winters just about did her in, the cold just gets right into your bones at our age. 

But anyway, yes, when I read that yellow bulletin, or when the ladies make their little comments during our walks, it's like they have this special, hidden meaning about my life tucked inside the words. I just know it's directed at me.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, or that someone is trying to control your actions or thoughts from outside?

No, no, I've never felt anything like that. My thoughts are my own, thank goodness. I mean, they might be watching me and sending those little messages, but nobody's putting thoughts into my head. 

Although, speaking of heads, I've been having the most terrible headaches lately. I think it's from my glasses. I went to Dr. Henderson—he's the optometrist over by the new grocery store, the one with the big organic section. Have you been there? The prices are just outrageous. Three dollars for an avocado! I remember when you could get a whole bag of them for that. But anyway, Dr. Henderson said my prescription hasn't changed, but these frames just pinch right behind my ears. I told him I wanted the wire frames, but he said the plastic ones are more fashionable now. Fashionable! At my age, I just want to be comfortable. I should have just gone to the place in the mall, they have those nice ladies who actually listen to you. 

But no, to answer your question, nobody is controlling my thoughts or putting things in my mind. It's just the messages in the bulletin and on the track that bother me.
Do you feel that other things in your environment—like things on TV, songs playing in the background, or things you read online—are also sending you special messages meant just for you?

Well, no, not the television or the radio. I don't really use the internet much, either. My grandson, Tyler, he tried to set me up with one of those tablet things for Christmas last year. He said, "Grandma, you can read all your books on here and play games!" But the screen is just so shiny, and my fingers never seem to press the right buttons. He spent three hours trying to show me how to check my email. Three hours! And he's such a smart boy, studying engineering at the state college. They just raised the tuition there again, my daughter was telling me. It's a shame how much it costs for young people to get an education these days. When my husband went to trade school, he paid for it by working part-time at the hardware store. You just can't do that anymore. 

But no, it's not the TV or anything like that. Like I said before, I really just came in because... well, even on my better days, I just can't shake this feeling that some people at church and in the walking club are watching me. It's just them, putting those little messages about me in the bulletin or in what they say when we're walking. It's not the television. Just the church and the walking club.
Outside of church and your walking club, have you ever felt that random events, strangers' actions, or everyday occurrences were directed at you or had a special meaning for you?

No, not really. It's not strangers or random things like that. It's just like I was saying, I came in because even on my better days, I just can't shake the feeling that some people at church and in the walking club are watching me. And then they put those little messages about me in the bulletin or in what they say. 

It's funny you mention strangers, though, because just the other day I was at the post office to buy some stamps. They have those new ones with the flowers on them, the botanical series? They are just lovely. I always try to get the pretty stamps for my letters to Tyler. Anyway, the line was just out the door. There was this young man in front of me, tapping his foot and looking at his watch every five seconds. People are in such a rush these days, nobody has any patience. He dropped a receipt and didn't even notice, so I picked it up and tapped him on the shoulder, and he looked at me like I had two heads! Just snatched it back without even a thank you. Manners have just gone completely out the window. My mother would have tanned my hide if I ever acted like that in public. She was a strict woman, my mother. Kept an immaculate house, though. You could eat off her floors. 

But no, I don't think that young man or anyone else was doing anything that meant something special about me. It's really just the people at the church and the walking club.

When you say people are sending you messages in the church bulletin or during your walks, do you actually hear or see something specific that others don't, or are you interpreting things that are really there in a special way that feels personal to you?

Well, the messages in the bulletin are definitely printed right there on the paper, anyone can read them. They just mean something different to me, you know? But... well, since you're asking about hearing things... sometimes, when I'm home alone and the house is just perfectly quiet, I'll hear my name. Or just a few words, and it sounds exactly like one of my friends from the walking club. It'll come from the kitchen, or maybe out on the back porch. 

Oh, my back porch! I've been trying to get someone to look at the screen door out there for three weeks. The wind caught it during that terrible storm we had last month—the one that knocked down Mrs. Gable's oak tree. Such a shame about that tree, it must have been a hundred years old. The city came out with those big woodchippers, made an awful racket for two straight days. You couldn't even hear yourself think! Anyway, the hinges on my screen door are all bent now, and it won't shut properly. I called the handyman, Mr. Davis, but he's always so busy. He said he'd come by last Tuesday, and I waited all morning, didn't even go to my water aerobics class, and he never showed up. 

But yes, sometimes I hear that voice from the porch or the kitchen, and it's so clear, I actually answer back! I'll say, "I'm in the living room!" before I catch myself and remember that I'm completely alone in the house. It's a very strange feeling.

Outside of what you’ve described with the church bulletin and your walking club, have you ever had other unusual beliefs that turned out not to be true, such as thinking someone was following you when they weren’t, or that you had a special connection to someone famous or important?

No, no, nothing like that. I've never thought I knew anyone famous. The most famous person I ever met was the local news anchor, Tom Brokaw—no, not the national one, Tom Bradley. He came to cut the ribbon when they opened the new grocery store on 5th Street back in... oh, it must have been 1998. They had free hot dogs and balloons for the kids. Tyler was just a toddler then, and he cried because his balloon popped on a rose bush. I had to go back and ask the manager for another one. The manager was so nice, a young man named Steve, I think. He ended up moving to Florida a few years later. Florida is just too humid for me, I don't know how people stand it. My sister went to Orlando once and said her hair was frizzy the whole trip. 

But no, I don't think anyone is following me or anything silly like that. It's really just what I mentioned before. I only came in because, well, even on my better days, I just can't shake this feeling that some people at church and in the walking club are watching me. And they put those little messages about me in the bulletin, or they slip things into what they say when we're walking. It's just them, nobody else.

Can you tell me more about how you know the messages in the church bulletin and walking club comments are specifically about you? Do you feel they are discussing you because of something you’ve done, or do you feel they have special knowledge about your thoughts or life?

Well, it's... it's hard to explain exactly how I know. I just know. Like when the bulletin talks about "finding your path," I know they mean me because of the walking club. But, you know, when I try to explain things like this to people, I start with one thought about the church or the mail, and then somehow I end up talking about quilt patterns. 

I used to quilt a lot, actually. The Double Wedding Ring pattern was always my favorite. It takes so much patience, all those little curved pieces. My grandmother taught me when I was just a girl. We'd sit on her porch, and she'd tell me about the birds. She knew every bird by its song. The cardinals were always the loudest in the morning. They say seeing a cardinal means a loved one is visiting you, which I think is just a beautiful thought. 

But anyway, I'll start talking about the church warnings or the birds, and then I can just see it in people's faces—they have absolutely no idea what I'm getting at. I just lose my train of thought completely. What were you asking me about again? Oh, right, if they know my thoughts. I don't think they can read my mind, no. It's just that the things they write or say are so specific to me, it couldn't be a coincidence.
Do you feel that the messages you're receiving mean that you have a special role, mission, or identity that others know about or are trying to tell you something about?

No, no, I wouldn't say it's a special mission or anything grand like that. I'm just a regular person. But... well, like I was saying before, I only came in to see you because I just can't shake this feeling, even on my better days, that some people at church and in the walking club are watching me. And they put those little messages about me in the bulletin, or they slip things into what they say. 

It's very unsettling, being watched. It reminds me of when my neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, got that new security camera. She put it right on the corner of her garage, and I swear it points directly at my driveway. She says it's for the neighborhood watch, but I don't know. Neighborhood watch used to just be people looking out their windows. We used to have meetings at the community center, and they'd serve those little sandwiches with the crusts cut off. Pimento cheese, mostly. I haven't made pimento cheese in years. You have to get the sharp cheddar, or it just doesn't taste right. 

But anyway, no, I don't think I have a special identity. It's just... they're watching me, and leaving those messages. I just wish I knew why they were doing it.

Have you ever felt that events, actions, or messages in the world around you—like things happening in public places, on signs, or in conversations—were directed at you or had a special meaning for you, even when other people didn't seem to notice it?

Well, like I was saying, it's really just the church and the walking club. I came in because, even on my better days, I just can't shake the feeling that some people there are watching me. And they put those little messages about me in the bulletin, or in what they say when we're walking. 

Walking is so good for you, you know. I try to get out every morning before the sun gets too hot. The dew is still on the grass, and the neighborhood is so quiet. You can hear the sprinklers going ch-ch-ch. My sprinkler head broke last week, actually. The water was just shooting straight up in the air like a geyser. I had to call my son Tyler to come look at it. He's so handy with those things. He works at the hardware store over on Main Street. They have the best selection of petunias in the spring. I always plant pink and white ones in the front flower beds. 

But, oh, what were you asking? Right, the messages. Yes, I just feel like they're putting those little messages about me in the bulletin and in their conversations. I don't know about signs or public places, just the church and the club.

It's just that the things they write or say are so specific to me, it couldn't be a coincidence.

No clear evidence of thought insertion, thought broadcasting, or third-person hallucinations, which might support schizophrenia spectrum disorders more strongly. However, given the chronic nature of the delusional themes without clear impairment in other areas of functioning, delusional disorder (F22.0) remains a strong candidate. Schizophrenia subtypes (F20.0–F20.9) cannot be ruled out without more information about functional decline, duration, or negative symptoms. The list remains unchanged at this point.

patient.answer:
No, no, I wouldn't say it's a special mission or anything grand like that. I'm just a regular person. But... well, like I was saying before, I only came in to see you because I just can't shake this feeling, even on my better days, that some people at church and in the walking club are watching me. And they put those little messages about me in the bulletin, or they slip things into what they say. 

It's very unsettling, being watched. It reminds me of when my neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, got that new security camera. She put it right on the corner of her garage, and I swear it points directly at my driveway. She says it's for the neighborhood watch, but I don't know. Neighborhood watch used to just be people looking out their windows. We used to have meetings at the community center, and they'd serve those little sandwiches with the crusts cut off. Pimento cheese, mostly. I haven't made pimento cheese in years. You have to get the sharp cheddar, or it just doesn't taste right. 

But anyway, no, I don't think I have a special identity. It's just... they're watching me, and leaving those messages. I just wish I knew why they were doing it.

patient.answer:
Well, like I was saying, it's really just the church and the walking club. I came in because, even on my better days, I just can't shake the feeling that some people there are watching me. And they put those little messages about me in the bulletin, or in what they say when we're walking. 

Walking is so good for you, you know. I try to get out every morning before the sun gets too hot. The dew is still on the grass, and the neighborhood is so quiet. You can hear the sprinklers going ch-ch-ch. My sprinkler head broke last week, actually. The water was just shooting straight up in the air like a geyser. I had to call my son Tyler to come look at it. He's so handy with those things. He works at the hardware store over on Main Street. They have the best selection of petunias in the spring. I always plant pink and white ones in the front flower beds. 

But, oh, what were you asking? Right, the messages. Yes, I just feel like they're putting those little messages about me in the bulletin and in their conversations. I don't know about signs or public places, just the church and the club.

inference.note: The patient's symptoms are consistent with Delusional Disorder, as they involve non-bizarre delusions focused on a specific theme (persecution and being watched by people in the church and walking club) without prominent hallucinations, disorganized speech, or grossly disorganized or catatonic behavior. Other schizophrenia spectrum disorders (e.g., F20.0–F20.9) have been ruled out due to absence of characteristic features such as thought insertion, broadcasting, or auditory hallucinations commenting on the patient. The delusions are not better explained by a mood disorder with psychotic features (ruled out based on presentation and lack of mood symptoms), and the content remains non-bizarre and circumscribed, supporting F22.0 as the most accurate diagnosis.
